newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia deputies tell Yeltsin to sign Nazi art law.
newsitem.headline: Russia deputies tell Yeltsin to sign Nazi art law.

text.p: The upper chamber of Russia's parliament urged President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday to stop resisting a draft law which proclaims Russian ownership over art seized by the Soviet Union from Nazi Germany during World War Two.

Deputies in the Federation Council voted overwhelmingly for a resolution rejecting Yeltsin's charges that there had been procedural irregularities when the law was passed and they sent it back to him for signing.
Both the Federation Council and the State Duma lower chamber have overruled Yeltsin's veto of the law, which has caused indignation in Germany.

The president refused to sign it as stipulated by the constitution, returning the document to parliament because of what he called "violations in constitutional procedures" in a reference to the postal ballot the Council used to override him.
The upper chamber said on Tuesday the vote was in line with internal rules and these could could only be challenged in the Constitutional Court.

Deputies also voted to send a letter to Yeltsin. The chamber's chairman, Yegor Stroyev, said the letter should mention the possibility of taking Yeltsin to the Constitutional Court if he refused to sign the law again.
